question.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ -1 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is orthogonal.
question.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\},$ $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\},$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{3}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{4\cdot (-1)+6\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 0+(-4)\cdot (-1)}{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{4\cdot 2+6\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-2)+(-4)\cdot (-1)}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{4\cdot (-2)+6\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot (-3)+(-4)\cdot 1}{(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ -1 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
